Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 46, verse 9–10:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾, meaning: I am not the first messenger. Al-bid' and al-badi' (the originator, the unprecedented) of anything is that which is newly begun. ﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you﴾. Ibn Ya'mar and Ibn Abi 'Ablah recited "ma yaf'alu" with a fatha on the ya'. Then there are two opinions regarding it.

(p-372) One of them: he intended by this what will happen in this world. Then there are two opinions regarding it.

One of them: "[When] the affliction intensified upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he saw in a dream that he had migrated to a land with palm trees, plants and water, and he related it to his Companions, and they rejoiced at this because of what they were facing of the harm of the polytheists. Then they remained for a while without seeing that, and they said: O Messenger of Allah, when will you migrate to the land you saw? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you﴾," meaning: I do not know whether I will go out to the place I saw in my dream or not. Then he said: "It is only something I saw in my dream, and I do not follow anything except what is revealed to me." Abu Salih narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise 'Atiyyah said: I do not know whether He will leave me in Makkah or expel me from it.

The second: I do not know whether I will be expelled as the prophets before me were expelled, or be killed as they were killed, and I do not know what will be done with you: will you be punished or be given respite? Will you be believed or be denied? This was said by al-Hasan.

The second opinion: he intended what will happen in the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from (p-373) Ibn 'Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed, after it was revealed ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2], and He said: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens...﴾ [al-Fath: 5] up to the end of the verse, so he was informed of what would be done with him and with the believers. It was also said: the polytheists rejoiced when this verse was revealed and said: Our affair and the affair of Muhammad are one and the same; and if he had not invented what he says, the one who sent him would have informed him of what would be done with him. So the words were revealed: ﴿That Allah may forgive you...﴾ [al-Fath: 2], and the Companions said: Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah, so what will be done with us? Then it was revealed: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens...﴾ [al-Fath: 5]. Among those who held this view were Anas, 'Ikrimah, and Qatadah. It is also narrated from al-Hasan.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if it is from Allah﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to its like﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions.

One of them: he is 'Abdullah ibn Salam. This was narrated by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, and it was the view of al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd.

The second: he is Musa ibn 'Imran, peace be upon him. This was said by al-Sha'bi and Masruq.

According to the first opinion, the mention of "its like" is an added element (silah), so the meaning is: and a witness from the Children of Israel testified concerning it, i.e., that it is from Allah, ﴿and believed﴾, the witness, who is Ibn Salam, ﴿and you were arrogant﴾, O assembly of the Jews.

According to the second, the meaning is: Musa testified concerning the Torah, which is like the Qur'an (p-374), that it is from Allah, just as Muhammad testified concerning the Qur'an that it is the speech of Allah, "and believed" whoever believed in Musa and the Torah, "and you were arrogant" you, O assembly of the Arabs, in refusing to believe in Muhammad and the Qur'an.

If it is asked: where is the answer to "in"? It is said: it is implied, and there are six opinions regarding its supposed wording. The first: its answer is: "Then who is more astray than you?", said by al-Hasan. The second: the sense of the speech is: and a witness from the Children of Israel testified to its like and believed; will you believe? Said by al-Zajjaj. The third: its supposed wording is: Do you feel secure from the punishment of Allah? Said by Abu 'Ali al-Farisi. The fourth: its supposed wording is: Will you not be destroyed? Mentioned by al-Mawardi. The fifth: Who among us and you is in the right and who is in the wrong? Mentioned by al-Tha'labi. The sixth: its supposed wording is: Have you not done wrong? This omitted element is indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, mentioned by al-Wahidi.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 46, verses 29–32:**

[p. 388] His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when We directed to you a company of the jinn﴾. God, mighty and majestic, uses this verse to rebuke the disbelievers of Quraysh, since the jinn believed in what they rejected. There are three opinions regarding the cause of their being directed to the Prophet (ﷺ).

The first: they were directed to him because of what occurred of their being pelted with meteors. Al-Bukhari and Muslim reported in their *Sahihayn*, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out with a group of his companions, intending the market of Ukaz. The devils had been prevented from the news of the heaven, and meteors were sent against them. The devils returned, and they said: 'What is wrong with you?' They said: 'We were prevented from the news of the heaven, and meteors were sent against us.' They said: 'That is only because of something that has happened. Strike the eastern and western parts of the earth and see what this matter is.' So the company that had turned toward Tihama passed by the Prophet (ﷺ), who was at Nakhla leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: 'This is what has stood between you and the news of the heaven.' Thereupon they returned to their people, ﴿and said: Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an, ﴾ ﴿guiding to righteousness﴾ [al-Jinn: 1–2]. God then revealed to His Prophet: ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened﴾ [al-Jinn: 1]." Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) neither recited to the jinn nor saw them. Rather, they came to him while he was at Nakhla, and they heard the Qur'an."

The second: they were directed to him in order that he might warn them, and he was commanded to recite the Qur'an to them. This is the view of a group, including Qatada. In the *Afrad* of Muslim, from the hadith of Alqama, who said: "I said to Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud): 'Who among you was with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn?' He said: 'None of us was with him. We missed him one night while we were in Mecca, and we said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has been seized or carried off. So we set out seeking him in the ravines, and we met him coming from the direction of Hira. We said: O Messenger of God, where were you? We had been anxious for you. Then he argued for the resurrection of the dead with His saying: ﴿Do they not see...﴾ to the end of the verse. Here "seeing" (al-ru'yah) carries the meaning of "knowing" (al-'ilm).
